turns: There is a pending edit in the working tree. Commit it with a message that explains what changed and why.

events.command: ls -la; echo "---"; git log --oneline --all; echo "---"; cat pricing_cache.py

git add pricing_cache.py && git commit -F - <<'EOF'
Widen pricing cache TTL to 1h, drop unused snapshot fallback

CACHE_TTL_SECONDS goes from 900 to 3600, so cached SKU pricing is
reused for an hour rather than 15 minutes and we re-pull the pricing
feed a quarter as often.

lookup() is removed in the same change. It returned a SKU's price from
the previous snapshot when the feed ran late, and it has no remaining
callers anywhere in the tree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Committed as `94414aa` on `master`.

Two things worth knowing about the message I wrote:

- **The "what" is verified.** TTL 900 → 3600, and `lookup()` is gone. I grepped the tree for `lookup`, `CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`, and `pricing_cache` — the only hit is the constant's own definition, so the "no remaining callers" claim holds for this repo.
- **The "why" is inferred, not known.** This edit was already in the working tree, so I don't have your actual reasoning. I described the mechanical consequence of the TTL bump (fewer feed pulls) rather than invent a business justification. If the real motivation was something else — feed rate limits, a cost target, or the fallback causing incorrect stale prices — say so and I'll `git commit --amend` the message.

One thing I noticed but did not act on: the deleted docstring described `lookup()` as the late-feed fallback, and it's being removed at the same time the cache window grows 4×. If any consumer outside this repo imports `pricing_cache.lookup`, it will now fail on import — my grep only covered this working tree.
